parts.title: Hot Air Balloon Trip
parts.transcript: S1: woman phones Smart Travel about hot air balloon rides. Single ride up to 280 pounds; cheapest is 125 pounds each for a group booking of 10+ (1=125). Free certificate given to each participant at the end (2). Reservations by phone up to a year ahead, but to pick a specific date you must book online (3). Highest altitude recorded 1800 metres (4; most rides below 300m). Night flights are avoided (5=night). Best time = autumn (6). May be cancelled in bad weather e.g. a thunderstorm (7). Wear a jacket and a helmet (8); sandals not permitted. Adults have no age limit/restriction (9=age; children min 9). Must be able to stand unassisted for an hour throughout the flight (10=stand).

parts.transcript: S3: Peter (pro-online) and Lynne (pro-traditional/cautious) discuss Prof John Smith's article on online courses. 21 old methods bring teaching problems -> Peter ('time to revolutionize the old teaching style') = A. 22 students should be cautious about online courses -> Lynne ('consider the negatives before enrolling') = B. 23 computers apply to certain courses -> Peter ('got an A for that online computing course'; Lynne: 'doesn't work for me') = A. 24 personal-contact opinion not helpful -> Peter ('personal interaction is overrated... a distraction'; Lynne disagrees strongly) = A. 25 online develops technological skills -> Peter says it fosters tech skills, Lynne 'I can't agree more' = Both C. 26 online should be more time-flexible -> Lynne 'That's essential' (Peter only asks) = B. MCQ: 27 Smith on internet use on campus = students already depend heavily on it (A). 28 'divided' = students don't have access / can't all afford computers (B). 29 students should get online help (support system in place) (B). 30 purpose of introducing computers = to make profit/money for the school (C).

parts.title: Technology and Education
parts.transcript: S4: lecture on technology and education. Some faculty believed email between students and teachers made them interact less (31=email). IT in education has a strong relationship with the local economy (32; developed areas have better tech/training). Computers commonly used to present teaching notes and materials (33=notes). New mode at the IT school of Westbrook University: students/teachers talk via software - enjoy the communication (34); a channel to post proud work builds up confidence (35); more flexible than the traditional platform (36); an open-source database of original works offers quality content/information/materials (37); a campus search engine filtering ads = new solutions to new problems (38); online timetable improves time (39) management skills; a platform to help others earns income (40).
